title: Dago on Twitter growth: batching content, link handling, credibility at 10K, and avoiding burnout
summary: Dago explains why he burned out after launching his course, how he batches two months of tweets in one week, and why links kill tweet reach unless you make people curious or incentivize engagement. He also shares how 10K followers changed perceived credibility, and why living and building real stories beats rehashing strategy.

principles.text: Too many open threads cause lost direction, lost productivity and burnout; clear the backlog to recover.
principles.quote: basically when I get too many things I get lost and I lose direction and when I lose direction I lose productivity and I burn out quickly

principles.text: Batch your content: go all-in for one week and write two months of tweets ahead of time.
principles.quote: I hide two months of content ahead of time let's basically just go all in for one week and write a ton of stuff

principles.text: Crossing a follower threshold like 10K boosts perceived credibility and directly lifts product sales.
principles.quote: reaching 10K for example was the biggest change in how people perceive me like it was crazy like it's just like the number of sales of my product just like improved overnight because people thought I was more credible

principles.text: Spend time building and experiencing things so you have fresh, raw stories to tweet about, instead of rehashing strategy.
principles.quote: it's better if I spend my time building or like experiencing [ __ ] and then tweeting about it then if I just like I did for the past year to spend all of my time tweeting

principles.text: Links hurt reach because people leave instead of engaging; make the tweet curious enough to engage without the link, or incentivize engagement.
principles.quote: if you put a link people will click on the link then they will visit the link and they will not engage with your Tweet and because they don't engage with your tweak it doesn't gives it more visibility and it dies

principles.text: Short subtitled clips (around 15 seconds) can drive podcast listeners from Twitter.
principles.quote: if you can get like a 15 seconds bite of the show with like subtitles and a cool bit that will probably do well
